changes: FIN's knob is now RATE on every sound, and is called RATE everywhere, LFO destinations too.
No more SMP RATE row or knob tap: fine tuning lives on TUN.
RATE starts at +63 (normal speed) on a new or cleared sound.
Sounds saved with FIN at +0 now load stopped: turn RATE up to +63.
TUN now turns 1 cent a step; press and turn for whole semitones. Reads like +3.07.
Fine tuning saves in the sound and plays the same on stock OS.
Tapping the knob between FIN and RATE no longer dips the speed or slides the pitch.
Uses less CPU when no sound has RATE on, leaving more time for the screen and pads.
No change to how RATE plays.
First library release, for Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74: FIN's knob becomes RATE, sound by sound.
RATE is pure sample speed, down to a stop and into reverse. Tap the knob, or check SMP RATE in SOUND SETTINGS, to switch.
Not yet tested on a unit: this exact build, two voices together, sound, scene and performance locks, and SOUND MANAGER.
Renamed Sample Playback Rate (was Sample RATE), and the module page now credits the author as Nathaniel Pavel (@npp1993). No change on the unit.
